subject: Re: Dedicated GPU headroom, burst governance and autoscale SLAs — Nova Enterprise onboarding
messages:
From: Naomi Roberts <naomi@nova-enterprise.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@helios.ai
Date: 2028-03-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — initial sizing for Pilot + Burst windows

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We kicked off an internal run-rate projection for the pilot and need a short write-up from Redwood with your recommended dedicated slab sizing and the burst/autoscale guardrails we should negotiate with procurement. Key constraints:
- Production latency 95p token < 300ms for chat workloads (seq len ~1024)
- Expected peak concurrency for pilot: 350 concurrent sessions over 2–4 hour windows, twice weekly
- Long tail: occasional spikes up to ~700 sessions for short promos; we want to avoid throttling for high-value customers

Can you give a recommended slab, a headroom percentage for guaranteed capacity, and a proposed policy for burst fallback (what falls back to cheaper model variants, preemptible pool, or degraded SLO)? Also share any calc spreadsheets and the typical lead time for provisioning additional GPUs if we need to upscale.

Appreciate quick guidance — procurement deadline is 2028-04-01.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Cloud Platforms
Nova Enterprise

[Attachment: pilot_traffic_sample.csv]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Roberts <naomi@nova-enterprise.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — initial sizing for Pilot + Burst windows

Hi Naomi — thanks for the details and the sample. I ran a quick back-of-envelope and attached a spreadsheet with the worked numbers (nova_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) and a short PDF summary. High level recommendations:

- Baseline dedicated slab: 32 A100-equivalent GPUs (estimate ~350 sustained concurrents at 1024 seq with our optimized runtime and 8-way batching).
- Guaranteed headroom: reserve an extra 20% (i.e., effective committed pool = 32 + 6 = 38 GPUs) as the contractual safety margin to maintain 95p latency SLO during predictable surges.
- Burst policy (proposed): allow up to 2x transient burst above committed pool using two layers: 1) Ephemeral on-demand instances from Redwood Dedicated shoulder pool (non-committed GPUs) for up to 2 hours per burst, and 2) Graceful fallback to a quantized 4-bit model variant for non-critical sessions when the shoulder pool is exhausted.
- Eviction & prioritization: VIP customer sessions (tagged via token) are pinned and will not be evicted; non-tagged sessions will be subject to queueing or fallback.
- Autoscale cooldown: 10 minutes to scale up, 30 minutes to scale down to avoid oscillation for promo spikes.
- Lead time for committed capacity: 2–4 weeks for provisioning reserved slab; ephemeral shoulder capacity is available immediately subject to regional availability.

I attached a policy YAML (proposed-autoscale-policy.yaml) that encodes the trunk/burst tiers and priority rules. Marcus, can you confirm the performance estimate and whether a 20% headroom is conservative enough given our current kernel selection for 1024-length chat loads? Priyom, I'll need your input on discounting & monthly commit language for the 20% headroom.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

[Attachments: nova_capacity_model_v2.xlsx, headroom_calcs.pdf, proposed-autoscale-policy.yaml]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Naomi Roberts <naomi@nova-enterprise.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — initial sizing for Pilot + Burst windows

On Wed, Mar 22, 2028 at 12:02 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com> wrote:
> I attached a spreadsheet with the worked numbers...

Naomi / Rishi — quick technical check from infra: the 32 A100-eq baseline + 20% headroom is reasonable for the pilot with the following caveats:

- Our throughput numbers assume continuous 8-way batching and KV prefix caching for chat. If Nova's session patterns have higher interactivity (lots of short sessions with few tokens), effective throughput will drop — we'd see higher GPU-per-session ratios.
- Shoulder pool availability depends on region. If Nova requires a specific region (e.g., us-west-2), the shoulder pool may be smaller and we should increase the committed headroom to 30% or introduce scheduled burst windows.
- For fallback quantized variants: latency improves but quality drift is non-trivial for few-shot prompts. Recommend an opt-in tag for sessions that can accept quantized fallbacks.

Operational suggestions:
- Add a scheduled burst window for marketing promos (we can pre-warm caches + increase batch sizes) to reduce transient pressure.
- Autoscale rule tweaks: use request-weighted scoring rather than raw concurrent session counts to avoid oversized scale-ups on low-token sessions.

I'll upload a microbenchmark summary into the shared doc link and include estimated tail-latency percentiles under different session mixes.

—Marcus
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: headroom_calcs.pdf]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Roberts <naomi@nova-enterprise.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — initial sizing for Pilot + Burst windows

Naomi — quick commercial note: the 20% guaranteed headroom can be structured two ways:

1) Commit + buffer: Nova pays for a committed 38-GPU slab at a discounted reserved rate; Redwood guarantees the headroom as SLA-backed capacity. Overage during bursts uses on-demand shoulder pool pricing with a cap.
2) Commit + credits: Nova commits to 32 GPUs; we provide a monthly headroom credit (equivalent of 6 GPUs) that can be consumed during bursts with fixed uplift pricing.

For procurement speed, option 2 is faster to contract (less procurement friction) and gives Nova the perceived flexibility while allowing Redwood to manage shoulder pool economics. I'll put a short redline for both approaches and send to legal if you want to proceed.

Also, we can add a clause for scheduled promotional bursts (60–120 minute pre-warm) with a lower uplift price.

—Priyom
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: commercial_terms_snapshot.docx]

From: Naomi Roberts <naomi@nova-enterprise.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-23T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — initial sizing for Pilot + Burst windows

Thanks — this is great, and aligns with procurement priorities. A few follow-ups before I loop legal:

- We prefer Option 2 (commit + credits) to avoid a large up-front reserved spend for the pilot. Please send the exact credit accounting and uplift multipliers for shoulder usage.
- Can you ring-fence VIP sessions by customer ID? We'll provide a mapping of our enterprise tenants to protect them from fallback.
- For the regional risk Marcus mentioned: Nova needs the committed slab in us-west-2. If shoulder capacity is constrained there, we are open to scheduled cross-region failover to us-east-1 for non-VIP traffic. Any latency implications?

If you can mail a short commercial appendix + the DocuSign-ready SOW by EOD Monday (2028-03-27 PDT), procurement will be able to hit the April 1 deadline.

Regards,
Naomi
Director, Cloud Platforms
Nova Enterprise

[Attachment: none]
